title: Prefill/decode pipeline: chunked speculative prefill, stage-overlap, kernel scheduler + KV-cache optimizations
author: Ava Mitchell
description: Context: This PR implements a coordinated set of runtime changes to improve prefill vs decode pipeline throughput and tail-latency for multi-tenant serving. Motivation: production telemetry shows wasted GPU cycles on long prefill sequences and spikes in tail latency when large batches interact with KV-cache eviction and kernel scheduling. This change set introduces chunked prefill, speculative prefill, stage-overlap scheduling between prefill and decode stages, a priority-aware kernel scheduler, and KV-cache eviction tuning to reduce redundant compute and improve continuous batching efficiency. Summary of changes: 1) Chunked prefill: split long prefill sequences into configurable chunks so that prefix KV-cache can be materialized incrementally and downstream decode work can begin sooner. 2) Speculative prefill: when downstream capacity is available we launch speculative prefill chunks to hide memory and I/O latency; speculative results are reconciled on canonical prefill completion. 3) Stage-overlap scheduler: enables overlapped execution of prefill and decode stages across micro-batches while preserving correctness of KV-indexing. 4) Priority-aware kernel scheduler: schedules attention and matmul kernels prioritizing low-latency tokens and hot KV-entries; introduces per-stream priorities and softer preemption to reduce tail latency. 5) KV-cache optimizations: improved eviction heuristics, batch-aware pinning for recent prefixes, and compact encoding for chunked-prefill indices. 6) Continuous batching improvements: better pack/unpack logic for chunk boundaries and a new throttling policy to maintain latency SLOs under bursty traffic. Benchmarks: On internal benchmark harness (gpt-like 7B/13B workloads) we observe median latency improvement of 15-22% for mixed prefill/decode workloads, p95 latency reduced by 30-45%, and overall token throughput increased by 12-18% depending on sequence mix. Cost analysis: estimated per-token GPU time reduced ~12% in steady-state, with larger wins on workloads with long prefixes. Backcompat & safety: all new runtime flags are off by default; feature gated under runtime.experimental.prefill_pipeline_v2. Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated nodes for 48h, then progressive rollout with telemetry gates. Checklist: - [x] Kernel changes validated with unit+perf tests - [x] KV-cache eviction unit tests and integration tests - [x] E2E perf harness runs and dashboard updates - [x] Feature flag + config defaults - [x] Migration notes in release notes Related work: builds on prior prefill/decode overlap PRs (see pr-67890, pr-71234, pr-77110) and kernel scheduler prototypes (pr-48612).
